claims.claim: names work as two parts: an angle word (leg, cover, mid-wicket, point) and a distance word (silly, short, deep, long)
short = closer to the batter; deep or long = farther
silly = so close to the batter that it is dangerous
square = level with the batter, across the pitch
fine = behind the batter, closer to the line of the pitch (the opposite of square)
claims.value: behind, near the line of the pitch

claims.claim: point, cover, mid-off are off-side positions
mid-on, mid-wicket, square leg are leg-side positions
fine leg is behind square on the leg side; third man is its off-side counterpart
slips are numbered outwards from the wicket-keeper; together the slip cordon
gully is squarer than the slips, on the off side
claims.value: squarer than the slips, off side
